--- 04/04/2025 Office Visit --- 
S: Mr. Hamilton presents for his annual physical follow-up visit. He reports feeling generally well. He denies any recent episodes of malar rash, photosensitivity, or joint pains. He also reports no new or worsening symptoms related to his systemic lupus erythematosus. 
O: BP 130/83, Wt 147 lb, normal heart rate, and respiratory rate. Physical exam reveals no joint swelling, warmth, or erythema. Skin examination shows no malar rash. 
A: Mr. Hamilton is stable with his systemic lupus erythematosus. His current management is appropriate, and there are no new concerns. 
P: Continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily. Recommend continued monitoring for lupus activity. No new medications are needed at this time. Return to clinic in 3-6 months or sooner if any new symptoms develop. 

--- 04/28/2024 Office Visit --- 
S: Mr. Hamilton returns with a complaint of rash. He describes a diffuse, non-pruritic rash that appeared on his face and upper chest several days ago. He denies any associated fever, joint pain, or other systemic symptoms. 
O: BP 119/92, Wt 149 lb, normal heart rate, and respiratory rate. Physical exam shows a diffuse erythematous rash on the cheeks and upper chest, consistent with a malar rash. No joint swelling or synovitis noted. 
A: The rash appears to be improving. It is likely related to a mild flare of his systemic lupus erythematosus. 
P: Continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily. Recommend close monitoring and follow-up. No changes to current treatment plan at this time. Return to clinic in 3-6 months or sooner if any new symptoms develop.
